verified_key_information_units.information: Headline financial performance for 2025 versus 2024: order intake increased 37% to SEK 142M (from SEK 103M), net sales grew 11% to SEK 131M (from SEK 118M), operating profit improved to SEK -1.9M (from SEK -9.7M), profit after tax was SEK -2.5M (from SEK -7.7M), cash flow was SEK +3.7M (from SEK +6.8M), and no dividend was proposed.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report (page 19) and condensed income statement (page 19) show year-on-year comparisons for order intake, net sales, operating profit, profit after tax, and cash flow. candidate_sentences.text: Consolidated net sales for the full year 2025 rose by 11.1 percent to SEK 131.5 million, compared to SEK 118.4 million in 2024.

Order intake showed a robust increase of 37.5 percent, reaching SEK 141.6 million compared to SEK 103.0 million the previous year, supported by strategic deals including a major SEK 22 million order to an American food producer.

Consequently, operating expenses decreased, and operating profit significantly strengthened to SEK -1.9 million from SEK -9.7 million the previous year, with the operating margin improving from -8.2 percent to -1.4 percent.
After tax, the net loss for the year narrowed to SEK -2.5 million from SEK -7.7 million, yielding earnings per share of SEK -0.09 compared to SEK -0.27 previously.
The Board of Directors proposed that no dividend be paid for the 2025 fiscal year, matching the previous year.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operational impact of external challenges: geopolitical uncertainty suppressed demand in the largest segment (warehousing and logistics), a ~20% depreciation of the US dollar against the Swedish krona (affecting 74% of sales and gross margin), and customs duties on non-European components increased administrative costs and burden.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO letter (page 5-6) explicitly details geopolitical uncertainty, weak demand in logistics, currency effects (USD lost almost 20% against SEK), and customs duty impacts on inventory valuation and administrative workload.

candidate_sentences.text: During the financial year 2025, JLT Mobile Computers AB experienced strong commercial progress and sales growth despite a challenging external market environment characterized by geopolitical uncertainty and weak demand in its largest segment, warehousing and logistics.
Despite top-line growth, profitability was heavily impacted by currency fluctuations.
The US dollar lost nearly 20 percent against the Swedish krona during the year, while dollar-denominated sales accounted for 74 percent of total turnover.

Market factors also included ongoing tariff and customs concerns, which increased administrative burdens and investigation costs, though Swedish-manufactured computers remained exempt from US export duties.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic diversification into ports, construction, and mining equipment segments to reduce reliance on the weakened logistics market, with early results reported from increased focus in these areas.
